nodes.name: 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 - 2H MoS_2 lateral heterojunction
aliases: 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 - 2H MoS_2 lateral heterostructure

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows distinct surface morphology between 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 and 2H MoS_2 regions with monolayer thickness of ≈0.74 nm across the heterojunction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, atomic force microscope (AFM) images of the as-grown heterostructure show the distinct surface morphology between the 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 and 2H MoS_2 regions, whereas the thickness across the heterojunction remains a monolayer at ≈0.74 nm over the whole region (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman mapping shows characteristic peaks of 2H MoS_2 A_{1g} (404 cm^{-1}) and 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 E_g (154 cm^{-1}) phonons that clearly separate the two regions; A_g peak blueshifted by 4.2 cm^{-1} indicates Mo p-doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, Raman mapping for the characteristic peaks of 2H MoS_2 A_{1g} (404 cm^{-1}) and 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 E_g (154 cm^{-1}) phonons apparently separate the outer 2H MoS_2 from the inner 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 (Figure 1g,h).

properties.description: Schematic diagram of HER boost at heterojunction

nodes.characterization_summary: PL spectra show A and B excitons emission of 2H MoS_2 confirming its presence at the heterojunction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the 2H MoS_2 phonon modes of E^{1}_{2g} and A_{1g} appear through the heterojunction region, and A and B excitons emission of 2H MoS_2 in photoluminescence (PL) spectra arise (Figure 1j), confirming the presence of the heterojunction and 2H MoS_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: ADF-STEM reveals atomically sharp heterojunction with (220)_{ReS2} || (110)_{MoS2}; Mo substitutes 24-40% of Re sites in 1T' region near junction; ≈4% lattice misfit with high tensile strain (>10%) in 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 lattices.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ADF STEM image for the hexagon-shape heterojunction revealed an atomically sharp interface between 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 and 2H MoS_2 (Figure 2d). ... Mo atoms substituted Re atoms by ≈24% at region I and ≈40% at region II ... lattice misfit between the two materials was estimated to be ≈4%.

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM shows ≈40 meV work function difference with 2H MoS_2 having lower work function than 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2, facilitating electron transfer from 2H MoS_2 to 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The line profile of surface potential across the 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 - 2H MoS_2 lateral heterojunction reveals that the work function (Φ) difference between 2H MoS_2 and 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 is ≈40 meV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry shows the heterojunction has overpotential of -0.084 V at 10 mA cm^{-2} and Tafel slope of 58 mV dec^{-1}, best among all TMD catalysts tested.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 -2H MoS_2 lateral heterojunction reached a low overpotential of -0.084 V at a 10 mA cm^{-2} current density and 58 mV dec^{-1} Tafel slope.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows the heterojunction has the lowest charge-transfer resistance R_ct among all samples, indicating fastest electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 1T' Re_x Mo_{1-x} S_2 -2H MoS_2 lateral heterojunction shows the lowest charge-transfer resistance hence faster electron transfer during electrochemical reactions.
